subject: solve mode.status issues with SL approximation

messages.author: de99922251954296
messages.subject: solve mode.status issues with SL approximation
parts:
Good morning

Please excuse me for the likely cross-posting with a similar issue I had opened privately with the helpdesk, hope this is the right place to ask.

INLA apparently fails to locate hyperparameters mode when the Simplified Laplace approximation is applied (similar problem with Laplace approx as well); specifically it results result$mode$mode.status == 2.

When the Gaussian approx with VB mean correction is used for the same model it runs just fine. 
These are the priors used; the model is a multilevel bivariate ICAR with 3 connected components:

ctrl.family <- list(
  list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial = -4, prior = "loggamma", param = c(1e-3, 1e-3)))),
  list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial = -4, prior = "loggamma", param = c(1e-3, 1e-3)), skew = list(initial = -0.015, param = 4))))

Here is the function call (SL approx):

inla( y ~ 0 + CC1 + CC2 + CC3 +  X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 +
    f(idx.vector, model = inla.IMCAR.model(k = 2, W = W.scaled),
      extraconstr = list(A = A.constr, e = rep(0,6))),
  data = input_data, family = c("Gaussian","sn"),
  control.family = ctrl.family, control.fixed = ctrl.fix ,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute = list(config = T, cpo = T, dic = T, internal.opt = F),
  num.threads = 1, inla.mode = "classic",
  control.inla = list(strategy = "simplified.laplace", dz = 1e-6))

May I please ask what is this issue due to, and if  there is a way to fix it while still using the SL approximation?

Here I attach the R code, the full logfiles (VB: new version, SL: simplified Laplace in old version), and the input data to run the code. 

Thank you in advance
Best regards
LC

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] solve mode.status issues with SL approximation
parts:
its seems like the model is almost singular. it runs into issues immedidately,
complaining that the Prec matrix is (numerical) singular, but the 'safe=T'
option rescue it. the results for VB looks ok.

the SL has more problems, as the internal representation is more fragile for
these `numerical singular models'. it still are able to rescue itself, when I
run it here, so I guess the advice would be to upgrade to R-4.4 and install the
most recent testing version. then retry


I would not recomment using the SL as the new take with the VB correction is
(almost uniformly) superior. my running times (1 thread) was 6 seconds compared
to 95, in favour of the VB


hope this helps
H

messages.author: de99922251954296
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] solve mode.status issues with SL approximation
parts:
Thank you very much for your reply!

I have done the upgrades. 

Now, the SL version does not even manage to recover anymore, but VB results are fine and computations are even faster than before.
I was reluctant to avoiding the SL approx since before the upgrade - when it managed to recover - it allowed for a slightly higher average (log-)CPO on more complex models, but apparently the only solution to make it work is centering y, so I'll follow your precious advice.

While we're at it, given that the model cannot run anymore with verbose = F (which allowed to save the logfile), may I please ask if INLA has another way to capture the full logs?

Thank you again
Best
LC
